skill.name: azure-postgres
skill.description: Configure Microsoft Entra ID authentication for Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server. Set up developer, group, and managed identity access, apply PostgreSQL permissions, and plan password-to-Entra migrations.
skill.summary: Configure passwordless Azure PostgreSQL access with Microsoft Entra ID.
skill.author: microsoft

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown links, portal URL examples, code fences, and legitimate Azure CLI guidance. The skill includes shell scripts that run administrative Azure and PostgreSQL actions; the main confirmed issue is unsafe SQL construction from caller-provided names. No prompt-injection text or hidden exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: Unsafe SQL construction from script parameters and identity names.
remediation.suggestion: Validate role names and database identifiers, escape SQL literals and identifiers correctly, or use psql variables with format functions before executing grants.

remediation.issue: Scripts can grant broad database privileges, including azure_pg_admin.
remediation.suggestion: Add dry-run output and explicit confirmation before admin-level grants or authentication-mode changes.

remediation.issue: Access tokens are exported through PGPASSWORD for psql sessions.
remediation.suggestion: Unset PGPASSWORD after each script, avoid logging command environments, and document token handling expectations.

semantic_findings.title: Unsafe SQL Construction in Administration Scripts
semantic_findings.description: The helper scripts insert command-line values such as users, groups, identities, and database names directly into SQL statements. A malicious or malformed value could change SQL executed by an Entra administrator.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited lines concatenate or interpolate script parameters and Azure-derived names into SQL strings. These scripts run as an administrative database user, so SQL injection or identifier confusion has high impact.

content.value_statement: Teams need secure PostgreSQL access without shared passwords. This skill guides Entra ID setup, managed identities, group permissions, and migrations for Azure PostgreSQL.
actual_capabilities: Explains Entra ID authentication setup for Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server.
Provides scripts for user, group, managed identity, and password migration workflows.
Documents Azure CLI commands for administrators, token acquisition, identity lookup, and server parameters.
Shows PostgreSQL functions for Entra role creation, group sync, and principal listing.
Includes troubleshooting checks for tokens, role names, DNS, firewall rules, and group sync.
limitations: Requires an Azure subscription and permissions for PostgreSQL, Entra ID, and target resource groups.
Scripts assume Bash, Azure CLI, jq, psql, and an authenticated Azure session.
Scripts do not fully sanitize database identifiers or role names before SQL execution.
Does not replace production change management, backup planning, or access review.

use_cases.title: Add Developer Database Access
use_cases.description: Grant a developer read-only, read-write, or admin access through an Entra ID user account.

use_cases.title: Connect Applications Without Secrets
use_cases.description: Map a managed identity to a PostgreSQL role so an Azure app can connect without stored passwords.

use_cases.title: Move Teams to Group-Based Access
use_cases.description: Use Entra groups to manage PostgreSQL permissions and choose the right group sync mode.

Do not disable password authentication until every migrated role has been tested with Entra ID.

faq.question: What does this skill configure?
faq.answer: It configures Microsoft Entra ID authentication and database permissions for Azure PostgreSQL Flexible Server.

faq.question: Does it create PostgreSQL servers?
faq.answer: It includes a basic create command reference, but its main focus is authentication and access configuration.

faq.question: Can it support managed identities?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a managed identity workflow that maps the identity to a PostgreSQL role.

faq.question: Can it manage team access?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents Entra group roles, group sync modes, and group permission grants.

faq.question: What tools must be installed for scripts?
faq.answer: The scripts expect Azure CLI, jq, psql, Bash, and an authenticated Azure session.

faq.question: Is it safe to run scripts automatically?
faq.answer: No. Review all parameters and SQL before running scripts because they can change database permissions.
